intervals.label: antihydrogen production run on LEAR
intervals.note: Production over "a period of three weeks" in September 1995 (CERN press release of 4 January 1996). End: LEAR "was closed in 1996" (CERN Courier, 17 August 2000); PS210's own last run date is not stated.
intervals.quote: In September 1995, Prof. Walter Oelert and an international team from Jülich IKP-KFA, Erlangen-Nuernberg University, GSI Darmstadt and Genoa University succeeded for the first time in synthesising atoms of antimatter from their constituent antiparticles.

intervals.label: completed
intervals.note: Completion is taken as the closure of LEAR; the collaboration's own end date is not stated.
intervals.quote: When CERN's low-energy antiproton ring (LEAR) was closed in 1996 after more than 10 years of operation

placements.note: Placed on the CERN Meyrin campus where LEAR stood (site:cern-meyrin, campus-grade); the experiment's own position on the ring is not given in a source consulted.
placements.quote: In September 1995, Prof. Walter Oelert and an international team from Jülich IKP-KFA, Erlangen-Nuernberg University, GSI Darmstadt and Genoa University succeeded for the first time in synthesising atoms of antimatter from their constituent antiparticles.

summary.plain: A xenon gas jet inside the storage ring and a chain of detectors downstream that recognised the unique signature of an antihydrogen atom.
summary.technical: Internal xenon gas-jet target in LEAR with downstream detectors identifying neutral antihydrogen atoms by their positron and antiproton signatures after the atoms travelled about ten metres.
